review_results.detail: New VerifiedLatestSnapshot binds deep-copied pointer and authenticated manifest to the ETag from the same original pointer read. A later HEAD cannot relabel an older verification with a newer generation.
Every cached reuse requires the exact ETag. Generation changes, including unchanged pointer body, rollback and disabled-run changes, force a new full verification.
After each newly performed full verification, the callback confirms the ETag again. A generation change during that pass clears the proof and fails closed without an unbounded loop.
Cache is a local variable of the automatic FVG invocation; the next invocation performs a new complete verification.

Each publication attempt clears the cached proof before work and in finally, including failed or uncertain publication. Post-publication verification rereads all municipality payloads even if pointer generation stayed unchanged.

Complete contract/hash/metadata validation remains in the publisher. Existing source-quality and checkpoint guards pass regressions; current coverage is checked using invocation time plus monotonic elapsed time, including cached no-op completion and pointer CAS.

Existing read_verified_latest API remains unchanged. Cache applies only to opt-in automatic FVG path; default-off/legacy and national worker regressions pass. No runtime schedule or deployment was changed by this verification.

Both new commands use repository-root working-directory above the backend default. The wildcard and -k selection run successfully under Python 3.13 with -S. No new dependency, trigger or scheduled CI job is required.

measured_local_read_reuse.measurement: Instrumented datastore get() calls against real 215-municipality contract fixtures; discovery and acquisition mocks were asserted unused.
measured_local_read_reuse.additional_evidence: A second invocation reads 215 again; a pointer generation change reads 430; forced post-publication readback reads 430 including the initial pass.

resolved_review_finding.problem: A fresh full read after cache invalidation could be superseded during that same read and then used without confirming its generation.
resolved_review_finding.correction: A cheap pointer/ETag confirmation now follows that full read; changed generations fail closed.

source_changes_after_test_start.change: Removed exactly one trailing LF byte after tests. Approved coordinator whitespace-only correction; no logic change and no repeat test required.

prior_evidence.role: Historical verification before the FVG cache change; this receipt covers the current source hashes.

limitations: Local deterministic fixtures and fault injection do not establish live GCS concurrency, latency, metering or deployment behavior. No real cloud job, scheduler, deployment or activation was performed by this verifier.

The cache assumes immutable published payloads. Direct administrative mutation/deletion of a payload after initial verification, without changing latest, is not continuously checked within the same no-op invocation; the next invocation or forced post-publication readback rechecks it.
Cheap pointer/manifest reads remain. The 645-to-215 result concerns municipality payload reads only, not total HTTP/GCS requests or a measured monetary saving.

The automatic-recovery rollout remains default-off and separately gated: quiesce legacy owners, verify cloud claims and readback, then consider explicit activation. Unresolved acquisition without a complete checkpoint still requires manual review; national crash before manifest remains outside automatic resume.
Existing acquisition/source-quality thresholds and bounded recovery windows are preserved. This verification does not extend late-cycle fallback, retries, monitoring policies or cost budgets.
No frontend/browser, real-phone, Safari/iPhone, minified Android, Web release or Play artifact qualification is claimed. No new app build was needed for this server-side producer change.
Remote PR CI and any subsequent promotion are owned by the coordinator and are not attested by these local test results.
PowerShell captures unittest stderr with native-command presentation in logs; the recorded process exit codes and unittest summary are all successful.
